newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian union leader says strike near end - agency.
newsitem.headline: Indian union leader says strike near end - agency.

text.p: An Indian trade union leader was quoted as saying a three-day nationwide strike by more than one million telecommunications and postal workers was likely to be called off on Friday.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted O.P. Gupta, secretary general of the National Federation of Telecom Employees, as saying trade unions were convinced the government would accept their demands in a wage row.
Gupta spoke to PTI on behalf of six unions representing government telecommunications and postal workers.

Striking telecommunications, postal and income tax workers employed by the government are demanding the elimination of a ceiling on annual bonus payments, arguing that a cap on bonuses for railway workers had already been lifted.

Gupta said the unions were convinced after meeting Communications Ministry officials on Friday morning that the ceiling on annual bonuses, currently set at 3,500 rupees ($100), would be raised. He said the strike was likely to be called off after union leaders meet later on Friday.
But Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's cabinet was not expected to take a decision until next week when the prime minister was scheduled to return from a visit to remote northeastern India, PTI said.
